transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-09-06
Start time: 17:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (CEO), Marcus Lee (CTO), Priya Singh (VP Product), Leah Ortiz (Head of People), Ravi Patel (Head of Sales Ops), Jordan Kim (Head of Infra), Sofia Martinez (Head of Research), Noah Green (Head of Customer Success), plus company-wide attendees

Summary:
Quick company update covering product launches, reliability incidents and learnings, hiring/human resources updates, GTM highlights, and a forward-looking roadmap for Q4. Short Q&A and wrap with action items.

Topics:
- Product: routing, batching, Dedicated updates, Redwood Optimize features
- Reliability: incident recap, KV cache bug and mitigation, rollout practices
- People: hiring, org changes, upcoming retreats
- GTM: topline, new enterprise logos, pricing conversation patterns
- Ops: security and compliance milestones (SOC2 renewal status)

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, happy September, quick housekeeping real quick, mute when not talking, we'll record, and we'll keep this to about an hour, ok?
[00:18] Audience: (applause, some cross talk)
[00:25] Avery Chen: All right Marcus, kick us off on product and reliability.
[00:30] Marcus Lee: Sure thanks Avery, hey team. Over the last month we've shipped smart routing 1.1, that includes new fallback policies and cost-aware routing. Early benchmarks look promising, 8 to 12% token cost reduction on mixed workloads, and latency SLOs held for 90% of traffic. There's still work on the canary rollout automation, we saw one regression in the KV cache path — unintended eviction on long chat sessions — which triggered slightly higher p99s for a subset of customers.
[01:05] Marcus Lee: The cause was a cache compaction race with our prefetcher, named prefetch-2, and the mitigation was to throttle compaction and add a short lock. Devs shipped a hotfix yesterday and it's in prod. The full post-mortem will be posted later today.
[01:30] Priya Singh: To add to that, the UX for model variant selection has been improved, meaning routing policies now expose a cost vs latency slider for customers in the console. We're also rolling out a Redwood Optimize suggestion engine in beta — remember that it's experimental, but it surfaced quantization suggestions that saved one customer about 22% on costs with negligible quality impact.
[01:58] Marcus Lee: Quick note, some of the transcripts call KV cache as 'KV cash' or 'KV cash-uh' in internal notes — just being real about how automated transcripts are messy.
[02:10] Member: (laughs)
[02:12] Leah Ortiz: On people — we've hired 14 engineers across infra and runtime this quarter, folks are onboarding, folks in growth will see new AE hires joining next week. There are a couple of org updates: Jordan will lead a new reliability pod focusing on inference edge cases and Priya will spin up a product team dedicated to cost tooling. Also, company offsite sign-ups go out today.
[02:40] Avery Chen: Great, thanks Leah. Ravi, where are we on trench sales and enterprise motion?
[02:46] Ravi Patel: High level, Q3 closed strong, three new logos in regulated verticals — one notable deal was with a healthcare platform, they chose Redwood Dedicated for data isolation and SOC2 plus HSM-based key management. Pricing sensitivity is still the main theme — customers ask tradeoffs: hosted vs dedicated, latency guarantees vs cost. We continue to lean on our benchmarks and the Dedicated reserved capacity story.
[03:20] Noah Green: On customer success, we've rolled out a new benchmark suite for customers to run their own workloads; a few pilots are hitting 99th percentile issues because of long context lengths, so SEs are working with them to tweak batching and prefix caching.
[03:40] Marcus Lee: Quick technical aside: some customers are running into p99 spikes with long multi-turn chat, we recommend aggressive prefix KV caching and shorter batch windows for low-latency routes. We'll publish a recommendation doc.
[04:00] Audience question: What about SOC2 renewal timing?
[04:05] Priya Singh: SOC 2 Type II audit is scheduled for Oct; we've closed the majority of the outstanding control gaps, but a few items in incident response need stronger runbooks. Ops will circulate the list.
[04:20] Jordan Kim: On infra — we invested in better kernel selection tuning, this gave us a 5% perf improvement on M60-like instances in lab. We also have better observability for model memory pressure which helped identify a mis-quantized artifact in a custom model loader.
[04:45] Sofia Martinez: Research highlights: the team's quantization experiments on Llama variants and a new per-layer quant profile are improving throughput on commodity GPUs. We also open-sourced a small eval harness for quality monitoring customers can reuse.
[05:10] Avery Chen: Ok, let's do a rapid-fire operations and legal update. Marcus? sorry, Priya.
[05:18] Priya Singh: Legal — we're making progress on a template DPA for EMEA customers to address data residency asks; procurement teams will have a draft this week. Also, for private deployments we've improved the on-prem install docs to account for air-gapped setups.
[05:40] Jordan Kim: For Dedicated customers, we've added a burst capacity config to better handle tail traffic without overprovisioning; it's in alpha and should be available next month.
[06:00] Audience mumble / side conversations
[06:15] Avery Chen: Ok Q&A — please drop questions in the thread. There's one about pricing for Dedicated and pilot commitments. Ravi?
[06:22] Ravi Patel: We're experimenting with a hybrid pricing approach — base reserved price plus usage multiplier for bursts; feedback from the pilot cohort will determine final model.
[06:35] Audience member: Are we seeing any feature flags or perf regressions from the new routing?
[06:42] Marcus Lee: Only the KV cache compaction race, everything else rolled out with dark-canary testing, which helped catch noise. We did temporarily see higher error rates for a small cluster because of a mismatch in quantized kernels but rolled back.
[07:05] Priya Singh: Product highlight — the new per-route dashboards went live for a few customers; this gives token-level cost breakdowns and traces for slow requests. Early feedback: customers love the visibility, want more downloadable reports.
[07:30] Sofia Martinez: Research is also working on eval-triggered alerts — you can tie a prompt set to a webhook that fires if quality drops. That'll be in Beta soon.
[07:50] Avery Chen: Quick finance snapshot — we beat plan on revenue but spend is higher in infra as we scale Dedicated capacity; CFO posted a note earlier with details. We are doubling down on Optimize signals to reduce unit cost.
[08:15] Audience: (questions from remote offices)
[08:30] Leah Ortiz: People update: folks are asking about parental leave, recap — updated policy is in the handbook and benefits portal, reach out to People ops for questions. Also, we're increasing stipend for conferences.
[08:50] Marcus Lee: Ops note — the recent incident was escalated properly, but we need better runbooks to avoid callback loops. I'll own the action to produce the mitigation checklist this week.
[09:05] Marcus Lee: (murmur) also follow-up: we'll add a canary metric that tracks KV cache eviction rates over time.
[09:20] Q from employee chat: What is the plan for open-source work and community contributions?
[09:27] Sofia Martinez: We'll keep open-sourcing evaluation infra and small training scripts, but core runtime optimizations will stay internal for now. Community repos will have clearer contribution guidelines.
[09:45] Avery Chen: Closing notes — hiring remains top priority, if you know great candidates refer them. Also, kudos to infra and research for the quant gains.
[10:00] Audience applause
[10:12] Avery Chen: Ok final administrative items: feedback survey will be live for 48 hours, please fill it out. We'll post the all-hands recording and the post-mortem links.
[10:28] Priya Singh: Quick reminder about the product roadmap doc update, please comment by Friday.
[10:35] Noah Green: Customer success will host a cross-functional sync for the healthcare pilot next Tuesday.
[10:45] Avery Chen: Thanks everyone, wrap up, see you in offices and remote.

(Conversation continues with smaller groups for ~50 more minutes in breakout rooms — but recording stopped after main session)
